newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Short Australia debt soggy,market mulls RBA report.
newsitem.headline: Short Australia debt soggy,market mulls RBA report.

text.p: *Short Australian debt futures weakened in early trading as the market lightened up some of its recent bullish expectations on a further policy easing in the wake of Tuesday's RBA report.

Short Australian debt futures weakened in early trading as the market lightened up some of its recent bullish expectations for a further policy easing in the wake of Tuesday's Reserve Bank quarterly economic report.

Bills and three-year bond futures started with a heavy tone after weakening in SYCOM, while the Australian dollar firmed as New York traders took heed to a Australian Financial Review article saying the RBA saw growth picking up and that there was no need for further rate cuts.
However, local economists felt that the outlook for policy was far from clear cut.

"The short end is pretty soggy at the moment, but when we get past this event and we start to get back into the data flow again, we get back into the same old story that the short end is well protected," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS.
"You are looking at a cash rate which is going to be no higher that 5.0 percent for some time to come, and conceivably could be lower," he added.
The RBA report was largely seen as a re-run of governor Macfarlane's Perth speech last week with the central back pushing for growth, but seeing no pressures from inflation or wages growth.

December bill futures, which had been pricing in a 25 basis point easing, fell to 95.16 just after the opening, but still equated to a cash rate of 4.84 percent compared to current 5.0 percent official rates.
The early weakness of the short-dated futures weighed on longer dated stocks, pushing yields slightly higher against the back drop of a fairly stable U.S. Treasury market.
The U.S. ended Tuesday narrowly mixed after the Federal Open Market Committee meeting left monetary policy unchanged as widely expected.

The local market underperformed against both the U.S. and New Zealand. However, it was reasonably steady against Canada, which came under pressure on Tuesday as the Canadian dollar fell after their CPI proved tame, and was seen lessening the need for a further tightening by the BOC.
